In the sequel of this paper, we will use the lower case letters (e.g., x ) to represent scalars, lower case bold letters (e.g., x ) to denote column vectors, bold-face upper case letters (e.g., X ) to denote matrices, and upper case calligraphic letters (e.g., X ) to denote sets. [E4] (text, Section C, page 6): The overall architecture of F AKE D ETECTOR corresponding to the case study shown in Figure 3 is provided in Figure 5. Besides the HFLU feature learning unit model, F AKE D ETEC - TOR also uses a gated diffusive unit (GDU) model for effective relationship modeling among news articles, creators and subjects, whose structure is illustrated in Figure 4. Formally, the GDU model accepts multiple inputs from different sources simultaneously, i.e., x i , z i and t i , and outputs its learned hidden state h i to the output layer and other unit models in the diffusive network architecture. Here, let’s take news articles as an example. Formally, among all the inputs of the GDU model, x i denotes the extracted feature vector from HFLU for news articles, z i represents the input from other GDUs corresponding to subjects, and t i represents the input from other GDUs about creators. Considering that the GDU for each news article may be connected to multiple GDUs of subjects and creators, the mean ( · ) of the outputs from the GDUs corresponding to these subjects and creators will be computed as the inputs z i and t i instead respectively, which is also indicated by the GDU architecture illustrated in Figure 4. For the inputs from the subjects, GDU has a gate called the “forget gate”, which may update some content of z i to forget. The forget gate is important, since in the real world, different news articles may focus on different aspects about the subjects and “forgetting” part of the input from the subjects is necessary in modeling. [E5] (text, Section F, page 2): The remaining paper is organized as follows. At ﬁrst, we will introduce several important concepts and formulate the fake news detection problem in Section II. Before introducing the proposed framework, we will provide a detailed analysis about fake news dataset in Section III, which will provide useful signals for the framework building. The framework F AKE D ETECTOR is introduced in Section IV, whose effectiveness will be evaluated in Section V. These claims failed the checks; write corrected claims to replace them:
- "The GDU model in the FAKEDETECTOR framework accepts multiple inputs from different sources simultaneously, including extracted feature vectors from HFLU, and outputs its learned hidden state to the output layer and other unit models in the diffusive network architecture.": support check: The cited evidence in E4 (Section C) mentions that the GDU model accepts inputs x_i, z_i, and t_i simultaneously, but it does not specify that these inputs are extracted feature vectors from HFLU. The claim also mentions that the GDU model outputs its learned hidden state to the output layer and other unit models in the diffusive network architecture, which is not directly supported by the evidence in E4.
- "The HFLU module in the FAKEDETECTOR framework is responsible for feature learning, as it is the input to the GDU model.": the quote is not in E4
- "The GDU and HFLU modules in the FAKEDETECTOR framework are illustrated in Figure 5.": support check: The cited evidence in E1 (Figure 5) only illustrates the architecture of the FAKEDETECTOR framework and does not specifically mention the GDU and HFLU modules. The claim states that the GDU and HFLU modules are illustrated in Figure 5, which is not supported by the evidence. [image]
